docs.title: Home
docs.text: Indicium standardizes one thing: the binding of a scientific claim to typed evidence and to the source that evidence points to, with provenance. A claim minted by any tool that imports Indicium has the same structure as one minted by any other, merges with it, and never travels without its evidence trace.

docs.title: Indicium
docs.text:
A standard for typed scientific claims bound to their evidence.

Quickstart Schema URI scheme

docs.title: One source of truth
docs.text: One LinkML schema generates the pydantic models, JSON Schema, SHACL shapes, the OWL ontology and the JSON-LD context. The supplemental SHACL shapes (constraints LinkML cannot express) are kept by hand beside it.

docs.title: Reused ontologies
docs.text: Evidence types come from ECO, citation relations from CiTO, document types from DoCO, IAO and FaBiO, the assertion structure from SEPIO, provenance from PROV-O.

docs.title: SHACL validation
docs.text: validate_graph runs the SHACL shapes over any RDF graph and returns the report. Domain packages add their own shapes through the same call.

docs.title: Reuse axes
docs.text: Axis Standard Evidence type ECO (Evidence & Conclusion Ontology) Claim to citation relation CiTO Source and document type DoCO and IAO Article type FaBiO Assertion and evidence structure SEPIO Provenance PROV-O Claim structure Bucur et al. 5-slot SuperPattern (K-CAP 2021)

docs.title: What Indicium defines
docs.text: Component What it is Claim The 5-slot Bucur SuperPattern (context, subject, qualifier, relation, object) with ECO-typed evidence Evidence A typed evidence record grounding a claim Source A DoCO/FaBiO-typed document or artefact that an evidence record points to CitationLink A CiTO-typed link from a source to a claim ClaimLink A CiTO-typed relation between two claims (supports, disputes, refines, ...) IndiciumDocument The container that serialises a set of claims, evidence and sources

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install indicium-standard

The 2.0.0 upload to PyPI is pending. Until pip install indicium-standard finds it, install from the repository:

pip install "git+https://github.com/HolobiomicsLab/indicium"

The distribution is indicium-standard; the import package is indicium

The PyPI name indicium belongs to an unrelated, abandoned key-value-store package that also ships a top-level indicium module. Installing both into one environment clobbers the import. Always depend on indicium-standard.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
import rdflib
from indicium import ASB_BASE, validate_graph

claim = f"""
@prefix asb: <{ASB_BASE}> .
<urn:claim:1> a asb:Claim ;
    asb:context "in vitro" ;
    asb:subject "compound A" ;
    asb:qualifier "inhibits" ;
    asb:relation "inhibits growth of" ;
    asb:object "cell line B" .
"""

conforms, report = validate_graph(rdflib.Graph().parse(data=claim, format="turtle"))
print(conforms)  # True

The Quickstart page continues with the typed model and the adapters.

docs.title: The name
docs.text: Indicium (Latin) is "a sign or mark that points to the truth"; in law, the evidentiary indication. Every claim carries its indicia, the traces that justify believing it.

docs.title: indicium.iri_bindings
docs.text:
Verified ontology IRIs for the indicium vocabularies.

Provenance: seeded from ASB semantic.py, then verified against EBI OLS4 / CiTO (plan Task 2). Update here AND in the LinkML schema meaning: together.

docs.title: Verification method
docs.text: ECO labels were fetched from: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/eco/terms?iri=http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ECO_ CiTO predicates were confirmed to resolve (HTTP 302 → 200) at: http://purl.org/spar/cito/

docs.title: Changes vs. ASB semantic.py
docs.text:
• citation: ECO:0000305 → ECO:0000033 Old label: "curator inference used in manual assertion" (wrong branch — this is under inferential/curator-inference, not literature citation). New label: "author statement supported by traceable reference" — an author assertion whose support can be traced to a cited reference; this is the standard GO/ECO code for evidence derived from a published source.

  • inference: ECO:0000001 → ECO:0000361 Old label: "inference from background scientific knowledge" — a leaf under ECO:0000205 (curator inference) → ECO:0000361. It is too specific (curator only) and was incorrectly described in the task spec as the root. New label: "inferential evidence" — the direct child of ECO:0000000 (root "evidence") that heads the entire inference/reasoning branch. Using the upper-level branch term is correct for a vocabulary binding that must subsume all forms of computational, logical, and manual inference.

  • speculation: ECO:0007672 → ECO:0000034 Old label: "computational evidence" — entirely wrong; this is about computer-generated data, not hypothetical assertions. New label: "author statement without traceable support" — an assertion not associated with results presented or a cited reference. This is the closest available ECO upper-level term for a speculative/hypothetical claim. ECO does not have a dedicated "speculation" class; this is the best match.

All other terms (data, knowledge) are retained with confirmed labels.

docs.title: indicium.verify
docs.text:
Quote verification kernel — match an LLM-extracted quote against source text.

Pure-Python, dependency-light, never raises. Shared across projects that ground claims / parameters / failure-modes in source passages (Perspicacité, ASB).

Additive to the indicium standard: this module adds a verifier verb alongside the existing data model (Evidence.quote_exact / TextQuoteSelector). It does NOT touch generated/model.py, the SHACL shapes, or any enum.

VerificationResult also carries a char_span — (start, end) offsets into the matched candidate's original (un-normalized) text — so callers can highlight or re-slice the exact source region instead of re-searching for it.

verify_quote(..., punctuation_flexible=True) adds an opt-in pass that matches a quote's alphanumeric tokens in order across arbitrary punctuation/whitespace (e.g. "P=0.001" ~ "P = 0.001,"), so a verbatim-modulo-punctuation quote verifies instead of degrading to a sub-threshold LCS. This mirrors ASB claim_ledger's token-sequence matcher, letting both projects share one kernel.

docs.title: verify_quote(quote: str, candidates: Sequence[str], *, near_threshold: float = 0.9, punctuation_flexible: bool = False) -> VerificationResult
docs.text:
Verify quote against candidates (source passage texts).

Outcomes
  • verified: quote is contained in some candidate (whitespace-flexible, case-sensitive). quote_exact = the candidate's verbatim span; score = 1.0; char_span = (start, end) offsets into that candidate's original text.
  • repaired: no containment, but the longest common substring vs the best candidate clears near_threshold (ratio over len(normalized quote)). quote_exact = that LCS region from the candidate; score = ratio; char_span best-effort (the normalized span is re-located in the original candidate; may be None).
  • unverified: nothing clears the threshold (likely paraphrase/hallucination). matched_index = quote_exact = char_span = None; score = best below-threshold ratio (0.0 when quote/candidates are empty or share no run).

With punctuation_flexible=True, an opt-in pass between containment and LCS matches the quote's alphanumeric tokens in order across arbitrary punctuation (e.g. "P=0.001" ~ "P = 0.001,"); a hit is verified, score 1.0. Off by default so existing thresholds are unchanged.

Never raises: empty/whitespace quote or empty candidates -> unverified. Ties resolved by highest score, then lowest index.

docs.title: ASTRA bridge (indicium.astra_bridge)
docs.text: Typed conversion between Claim objects and ASTRA insights. Needs the astra extra.

docs.title: indicium.astra_bridge
docs.text:
ASTRA ↔ Indicium bridge — convert between ASTRA Insight dicts and Indicium Claims.

Optional-extra-gated: pyyaml must be installed (pip install "indicium-standard[astra]" or pip install pyyaml). The pyyaml extra is already in the codegen extra and dev dependency-group, so it is always available during development.

Gap 6 implementation from the Indicium v1.3 design spec.

docs.title: claim_to_insight(claim: 'Claim', *, evidence_doi: str | None = None) -> dict
docs.text:
Convert an Indicium Claim to an ASTRA Insight YAML dict.

Mapping rules: - claim text: "{subject} {qualifier} {relation} {object}" (stripped). - evidence: DOI item if evidence_doi provided, else artifact item using claim id. - indicium_claim_ref: set to claim.id when present. - created_at: current UTC ISO timestamp.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default claim 'Claim'

Indicium Claim object.

required evidence_doi str | None

DOI to include in the evidence list. Optional.

None

Returns:

Type Description dict

ASTRA Insight dict (id, claim, created_at, evidence, indicium_claim_ref).

docs.title: insight_to_claim(insight: dict, *, analysis_id: str, source_doi: str | None = None) -> 'Claim'
docs.text:
Convert an ASTRA Insight dict to a best-effort Indicium Claim.

Mapping rules: - subject/object: split claim text at verb heuristic, or use full text as object. - qualifier: defaults to has_property; overridden when a known verb is found. - relation: same as qualifier_str (the matched verb phrase) or "has_property". - context: ASTRA scope field joined with tags; empty string if absent. - asserted_by: set to analysis_id. - astra_insight_ref: set to "{analysis_id}/{insight['id']}".

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default insight dict

ASTRA Insight dict (id, claim, scope, tags, …).

required analysis_id str

ASTRA analysis ID used as asserted_by and ref prefix.

required source_doi str | None

If provided, appended to context.

None

Returns:

Type Description 'Claim'

A best-effort Indicium Claim (some slots may be empty strings).

Project an indicium Claim onto the EvidenceSnippet dict of an ASB task card.

The target structure is the EvidenceSnippet class of the ASB task card schema, asb_schema/asb_card.yaml in the asb-schema package (asb-schema>=0.4.0). Its fields are snippet_id, source_path, reason and text. The module keeps its earlier name, indicium.adapters.scitask, so that existing imports keep working.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: 2.0.0 — 2026-11-01
docs.text: First public release. These breaking changes landed before any Indicium package release. Existing downstream records may still embed the earlier context.

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
• The asb: vocabulary base moved to https://w3id.org/asb#. It had two earlier bases. 1.x used https://asb.holobiomics.org/ns/asb#, a domain that was never registered, so a third party could have taken it and served arbitrary definitions for this standard's term IRIs. Indicium PR #4 (2026-06-14) then moved it to https://holobiomicslab.eu/ns/asb#, and 2.0.0 settles on the permanent w3id identifier. Every asb: term IRI therefore changes. The 2.0.0 SHACL shapes target the w3id IRIs, so they do not recognise a claim typed with either earlier base: such a claim goes unchecked instead of failing. Released data carries the intermediate base: the 106 indicium/*.jsonld files of the asb-skill-collections pre-release metabolomics-v0.1.0 (2026-06-22) bind https://holobiomicslab.eu/ns/asb# and do not validate against the 2.0.0 shapes. To migrate such data, bind the asb: prefix of its JSON-LD context (or rewrite its IRIs) to https://w3id.org/asb#; the local names are unchanged. Then validate it with indicium.validate_graph. Consumers that bind the asb: prefix themselves, notably the shape files in indicium-adapters-metabolomics, must be updated in lockstep.
  • The distribution is renamed indicium → indicium-standard. The import package is unchanged: import indicium still works. The PyPI name indicium is held by an unrelated, abandoned key-value-store package that also ships a top-level indicium module; installing both into one environment clobbers the import. Depend on indicium-standard, never on indicium.
  • Two SEPIO bindings are corrected before the namespace deposit. supports_claim now expands to sepio:0000427 (is_evidence_line_for), an evidence-line-to-claim relation, instead of the oppositely directed sepio:0000007. Skill reliance asserts now expands to indicium:asserts, declared in the LinkML schema, instead of sepio:0000130 (authored_by). JSON keys and the local for_claim predicate are unchanged. Refresh embedded contexts and regenerate previously expanded RDF. Supporting, disputing or inconclusive direction is a separate sepio:0000183 annotation; the historical supports_claim key alone does not establish that direction.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• LICENSE (MIT). 1.x declared MIT in pyproject.toml but shipped no licence text, so a wheel would have distributed MIT-claimed code without the required notice.
  • indicium.ASB_BASE, indicium.INDICIUM_BASE, indicium.asb_term() — the vocabulary bases are now part of the public API, read from the generated model's prefix map so they cannot drift from the SHACL shapes. Consumers that hardcoded the IRI kept validating against a dead namespace after the base moved: the shapes matched nothing and every graph reported conforms=True. Import these instead.
  • tests/test_namespace_base.py — guards against reintroducing an unowned namespace base, and pins the metadata lookup to the declared distribution name.
  • A reproducible JSON-LD context generated from the schema, shipped in the package and copied into the documentation site. OBO prefixes expand in JSON-LD 1.1; property IRIs and enum meanings now agree with the SHACL shapes.
  • Local release checks and a Trusted Publishing workflow with matching tag, package version and dated changelog checks before publication.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• __version__ reported the wrong version. It queried importlib.metadata for the distribution indicium, which after the rename resolves either to nothing (falling back to 0.0.0+unknown) or to the unrelated squatting PyPI package, reporting its version as ours. It now queries indicium-standard. The wheel-smoke CI job asserts the installed wheel reports the built version.
  • docs/changelog.md is now generated from this file (make docs-changelog) rather than hand-maintained. It had been frozen at 1.0.0 for twelve releases, and release.yml extracts its release notes from it.
  • Installation examples now consistently name indicium-standard, including its optional extras. Schema generation works on Linux and macOS.
  • The generated OWL ontology uses the namespace root https://w3id.org/indicium as its document IRI and carries the version and the licence (pav:version, dct:license), which the LinkML source now declares; the model and the JSON Schema carry the version too. RDF serialization is deterministic for release verification.
  • The published SHACL file, docs/schema-assets/indicium.shapes.ttl (a release asset), now holds the supplemental shapes as well as the generated ones, so a SHACL processor run on it agrees with validate_graph: before, it accepted a claim with neither qualifier nor domain_qualifier.
  • The sdist includes only package source, schema assets and release metadata; internal development plans are excluded.
  • The package metadata names its author, states the licence as the SPDX expression MIT with LICENSE as its licence file (instead of the full text in the License field), and lists Documentation and Issues URLs.
  • SEPIO binding regression tests use an attributed excerpt of the ontology's inverse, domain and range axioms. The documentation explains the target link, separate evidence direction and the local reliance predicate.

docs.title: Namespace registration
docs.text:
• Canonical bases remain https://w3id.org/indicium/ and https://w3id.org/asb#. The vocabulary deposit and redirects are prepared separately; registration does not create a hosted store of claim instances.
  • Prepared term redirects send HTML clients to https://holobiomicslab.eu/indicium/reference/<Name>/ and RDF clients to the vocabulary representation under /ns/indicium/. The reference pages must be live before the w3id registration is submitted.
  • ASB validation assertions use SEPIO_0000183 with SEPIO_0000403, SEPIO_0000404 or SEPIO_0000405, and RO_0002558 with ECO_0000501. These are external assertion annotations, not Indicium claim-status values.

docs.title: 1.12.0 — 2026-06-10
docs.text: • New SourceTaskKind enum {reproduction, analysis, component_reconstruction, extension} + optional Claim.source_task_kind slot (asb:sourceTaskKind) — a claim-level reproducibility-provenance qualifier, sibling of Evidence.workflow_coupling (Suter et al. 2025) at claim↔source-task granularity. Canonical replacement for ASB's out-of-schema asbext:source_task_kind. Added to context.jsonld for portability. Additive, backward-compatible; SHACL non-closed.

docs.title: 1.11.0 — 2026-06-03
docs.text: • New SSSOMMapping class (SSSOM term mapping) + IndiciumDocument.sssom_mappings collection, with a derived_from lineage slot (cthoyt 2026-05-29). Adds sssom/semapv/skos prefixes. Additive, backward-compatible.

docs.title: 1.10.0 — 2026-06-03
docs.text: • Evidence gains optional workflow_coupling (WorkflowCoupling enum: tight/loose/ad_hoc/unknown) — a reproducibility qualifier per Suter et al. 2025 (DOI 10.1016/j.future.2025.107974). Additive, backward-compatible; SHACL non-closed.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• VerificationResult.char_span — a 5th, defaulted field (tuple[int, int] | None = None) giving (start, end) offsets into the matched candidate's original (un-normalized) text. Populated for verified matches from the regex span; best-effort for repaired matches (the recovered span is re-located in the original candidate, and may remain None). Lets callers highlight or re-slice the exact source region without re-searching.
  • verify_quote(..., punctuation_flexible=True) — an opt-in pass between exact containment and LCS that matches the quote's alphanumeric tokens ([A-Za-z0-9]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9]+)*) in order across arbitrary non-alphanumeric padding, with per-token boundary guards. A hit is verified with score = 1.0 and a char_span spanning first-token-start → last-token-end. This recognises a verbatim-modulo-punctuation quote (e.g. P=0.001 ~ P = 0.001,) instead of degrading it to a sub-threshold LCS, mirroring ASB claim_ledger's token-sequence matcher.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: Lets ASB claim_ledger and Perspicacité consume one shared verification kernel: char_span carries the exact source offsets downstream, and the opt-in punctuation-flexible pass matches numeric/statistical quotes whose punctuation shifts between extraction and source. Backward-compatible and additive only: both changes are defaulted off / defaulted None, existing thresholds and the 11 prior kernel tests are unchanged, and there are no changes to generated/model.py, the SHACL shapes, or any enum.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• verify_quote kernel (indicium.verify, exported from the package root) — a pure-Python, dependency-light, never-raises verifier that matches an LLM-extracted quote against source passage texts. Returns VerificationResult(status, matched_index, quote_exact, score) where status is verified (whitespace-flexible, case-sensitive containment; recovers the source's verbatim span, score = 1.0), repaired (no containment, but the longest common substring vs the best candidate clears near_threshold, default 0.9), or unverified. Structurally guarantees unverified ⇒ matched_index is None; degenerate input (empty/whitespace quote, empty candidates, or None/non-str entries) degrades safely instead of raising.
  • Exported verify_quote and VerificationResult from the package root.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: Lets downstream projects (Perspicacité R3, ASB) ground claim / parameter / failure-mode quotes against original source text — verifying provenance and catching paraphrase or hallucination — without depending on rdflib or the generated model. Additive only: no changes to generated/model.py, the SHACL shapes, or any enum.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• domain_qualifier slot (slot_uri: asb:domainQualifier) — an OPEN, snake_case-patterned (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$) qualifier slot for domain-adapter vocabularies (e.g. transcriptomics aligned_with, differentially_expressed_in). This is the standard's side-channel for domain extensions, mirroring how enrichment terms ride on asb:*_ontology_term. The closed Bucur SuperPatternQualifier enum on asb:qualifier is unchanged — domain terms never pollute it.
  • QualifierPresenceShape (supplemental SHACL, sh:or) — a Claim must carry at least one of asb:qualifier (closed Bucur SuperPattern) or asb:domainQualifier (open domain extension).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • qualifier slot is no longer required on its own. A Claim previously had to carry a core Bucur qualifier; it may now satisfy the "at least one qualifier" rule via domain_qualifier instead. The closed enum and its maxCount 1 are retained; only the slot-level minCount 1 moved to the either-or QualifierPresenceShape.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: Resolves indicium#1 (reported by Dina, 2026-05-29). Domain-adapter qualifiers extended asb:qualifier directly, but that slot is a CLOSED 20-term LinkML enum (Bucur K-CAP 2021), so the generated sh:in shapes rejected every extended qualifier — blocking all domain adapters (metabolomics, metabokg, emi, transcriptomics) and the ASB benchmark. SHACL merges additively (validate_graph graph-union), so an adapter-side shape could never relax the existing sh:in; the fix had to live in the core standard. We chose to keep asb:qualifier pristine and route domain qualifiers to a new open slot (Reading 1) rather than dilute the published closed vocabulary.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Additive. v1.6 serialisations always carry a core asb:qualifier, so they still satisfy QualifierPresenceShape and remain valid. Consumers gain the domain_qualifier slot; no existing slot changed its slot_uri or range.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Package context.jsonld for downstream consumers. Move docs/context.jsonld into src/indicium/schema/context.jsonld (canonical location) and symlink it back to docs/ so mkdocs continues to publish it. Wheels now ship the file, so consumers can load it via importlib.resources.files("indicium.schema") / "context.jsonld".

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Claim aliases: predicate (alias for relation) and super_pattern (alias for qualifier) — explicit names matching the ASB spec.
  • Evidence aliases + new slots: quote_exact (alias for quote), supports_claim (alias for for_claim, mapped to sepio:0000007), quote_location (string locator), eco_code (range: EcoCodeAsbSubset).
  • EcoCodeAsbSubset enum — 8 ECO codes ASB emits (textual_quotation, computational_evidence, expert_curation, inference_from_background_knowledge, author_statement, experimental_evidence, combinatorial_evidence, traceable_author_statement).
  • Source slots: doi, paragraph_id, xpath_pointer — explicit forms of the InformationSource locators ASB targets.
  • SoftwareEntity class — new class for globally-identified tools (canonical_url, version, edam_operation, edam_topics, bio_tools_id). Added to IndiciumDocument.software_entities.
  • JSON-LD @context at docs/context.jsonld — stable mapping for downstream consumers. To be served at w3id.org/indicium/context.jsonld pending the w3id PR; currently published at holobiomicslab.github.io/indicium/context.jsonld.
  • docs/sepio-assertion.md — reference for the SEPIO assertion pattern (skill → claim).
  • docs/uri-scheme.md — reference for indicium:claim/<uuid> + content-hash citation variant.
  • tests/fixtures/asb_skill_roundtrip/ — canonical fixture consumed by Plan 1c's round-trip CI test in indicium-adapters.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: All Wave 1 changes are additive: every new slot is non-required and shares its slot_uri with an existing slot (where one exists). v1.5 serialisations remain valid; v1.6 consumers gain the spec-required names.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • extra_shapes keyword argument to validate_graph() — callers (e.g. domain adapters via SHACLProvider) can now inject additional SHACL shapes that are merged with the built-in schema shapes before validation.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• allow_warnings=True now passed to pyshacl in validate_graph() so that sh:Warning-severity shapes no longer set conforms=False; warnings are reported in the validation report text only.
  • Conditional SHACL constraint added: superseded_by is now required when claim_status = superseded.
  • Core types (Claim, Evidence, Source, and status enums) are now re-exported from the top-level indicium package for ergonomic imports.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • indicium.adapters.astra.claim_to_insight — use astra_bridge instead.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• IndiciumDocument container type for grouping claims.
  • superseded_by field on Claim.
  • Fixed ClaimLink URI generation.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ClaimLink, ClaimStatus types.
  • OA (Web Annotation) selectors for evidence provenance.
  • ASTRA bridge adapter.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Script and DataAsset classes for code/data artefacts as evidence.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Figure class and FigureType enum for figure-as-evidence support.

docs.title: indicium kernel contract
docs.text: A kernel is a small, shared, dependency-light module other projects build on (the reference example is src/indicium/verify.py, verify_quote). New kernels must meet this bar.

docs.title: Required properties
docs.text:
1. Pure-Python, dependency-light. Standard library only (re, dataclasses, difflib, typing). No third-party imports, no I/O, no network, no global state.
  2. Never raises. A kernel function returns a typed result for every input, including degenerate ones (empty, None, wrong-typed entries are coerced or mapped to a benign result). Defensive coercion is the only try/except, and it lives at one documented boundary — not scattered.
  3. One clear job, one frozen result type. A single public function (or a tiny set) and a @dataclass(frozen=True) result whose fields are documented inline. Structural invariants are stated (e.g. "unverified ⇒ matched_index / quote_exact are None").
  4. Additive / non-invasive. A kernel adds a verb; it must not edit generated/model.py, the SHACL shapes, or any enum. New result fields are appended with defaults so existing callers keep working.
  5. Backward-compatible evolution. New behavior is opt-in (a defaulted keyword param) and new outputs are defaulted fields. Existing callers' tests pass unchanged across the upgrade.
  6. WHY-not-WHAT comments; tight docstrings. Comments explain a non-obvious invariant or a coercion's reason. Docstrings state the current contract, not change history or commit hashes.

docs.title: Worked example: verify_quote
docs.text:
• ~165 lines, stdlib-only, one public function + one frozen VerificationResult.
  • Three outcomes (verified / repaired / unverified) with a stated tie-break and a documented "unverified ⇒ None span" invariant.
  • The only try/except-shaped defense is the None/non-str candidate coercion, with a comment explaining it preserves matched_index alignment.
  • 1.9.0 added char_span (defaulted field) and punctuation_flexible (defaulted param) additively — prior tests passed unchanged; the suite now covers the additions (17 tests).

docs.title: Checklist for a new kernel
docs.text:
• [ ] stdlib-only; no I/O / network / globals
  • [ ] returns a typed result for every input; never raises
  • [ ] single responsibility; frozen result type; invariants documented
  • [ ] no edits to model.py / SHACL / enums
  • [ ] new behavior opt-in, new outputs defaulted
  • [ ] WHY-comments; contract-only docstrings
  • [ ] full unit coverage incl. degenerate inputs

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Every Python block on this page runs, in order, in the test suite (tests/test_docs_examples.py).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install indicium-standard
# or, in a uv project:
uv add indicium-standard

Optional extras:

pip install "indicium-standard[astra]"     # ASTRA bridge (PyYAML)
pip install "indicium-standard[codegen]"   # regenerate the artefacts from the LinkML source

The 2.0.0 upload to PyPI is pending. Until pip install indicium-standard finds it, install from the repository:

pip install "git+https://github.com/HolobiomicsLab/indicium"

The import package is indicium. Never install the unrelated PyPI package named indicium next to it: both ship a top-level indicium module.

docs.title: Validate a claim
docs.text:
A claim is an RDF node of type asb:Claim with the five SuperPattern slots. Build the prefix from ASB_BASE rather than typing the IRI:

import rdflib
from indicium import ASB_BASE, validate_graph

claim_ttl = f"""
@prefix asb: <{ASB_BASE}> .
<urn:claim:c001> a asb:Claim ;
    asb:context "in vitro" ;
    asb:subject "compound A" ;
    asb:qualifier "inhibits" ;
    asb:relation "inhibits growth of" ;
    asb:object "cell line B" .
"""

conforms, report = validate_graph(rdflib.Graph().parse(data=claim_ttl, format="turtle"))
print(conforms)  # True

A claim without its subject, relation and object does not conform, and the report names each missing slot:

incomplete_ttl = f"""
@prefix asb: <{ASB_BASE}> .
<urn:claim:c002> a asb:Claim ; asb:context "in vitro" ; asb:qualifier "inhibits" .
"""

conforms, report = validate_graph(rdflib.Graph().parse(data=incomplete_ttl, format="turtle"))
print(conforms)  # False
print("asb:subject" in report, "asb:relation" in report, "asb:object" in report)  # True True True

validate_graph(data, extra_shapes=...) merges additional SHACL shapes, for example those of a domain adapter, into the base shapes before validating.

docs.title: The typed model
docs.text:
The pydantic classes are generated from the same LinkML source and re-exported from indicium:

from indicium import Claim, SuperPatternQualifier

claim = Claim(
    id="c001",
    context="in vitro",
    subject="compound A",
    qualifier="inhibits",
    relation="inhibits growth of",
    object="cell line B",
)
print(claim.qualifier is SuperPatternQualifier.inhibits)  # True

qualifier takes one of the 20 Bucur SuperPattern terms. A domain package may use domain_qualifier instead; the SHACL shapes require at least one of the two.

docs.title: The claim dict
docs.text:
The adapters take a plain dictionary:

Key Required Type Notes id yes str Stable identifier (e.g. "c001", a UUID, or a URN) context yes str Experimental or conceptual setting subject yes str Entity the claim is about qualifier yes, for the adapters below str One of the 20 Bucur SuperPattern terms relation yes str Free-text elaboration of the relation object yes str Target entity claim_type no str "explicit" or "implicit" source_excerpt no str Verbatim text from the source evidence no list[dict] Each item may carry doi, artifact, quote, evidence_type

Claim(**{k: v for k, v in claim_dict.items() if k != "evidence"}) validates the same slots and the qualifier enum (the model rejects the evidence key, which belongs to the adapter layer), and claim.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True) returns a dict the adapters accept. In the RDF model, evidence is a separate Evidence node linked to its claim.

docs.title: Project a claim onto other formats
docs.text:
from indicium import claim_to_evidence_snippet, claim_jsonld

claim_dict = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "source_excerpt": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.",
    "evidence": [{"doi": "10.1234/test", "quote": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%."}],
}

# EvidenceSnippet, as embedded in ASB task cards
snippet = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim_dict)
print(snippet["source_path"])  # doi:10.1234/test
print(snippet["reason"])       # compound A [inhibits] inhibits growth of cell line B (context: in vitro)

# JSON-LD node for KGmemory
node = claim_jsonld(claim_dict)
print(node["@id"])  # urn:indicium:claim:c001

The ASTRA bridge works on the typed model and needs the astra extra:

from indicium.astra_bridge import claim_to_insight

insight = claim_to_insight(claim, evidence_doi="10.1234/test")
print(insight["claim"])     # compound A inhibits inhibits growth of cell line B
print(insight["evidence"])  # [{'id': 'e1', 'doi': '10.1234/test'}]

indicium.claim_to_insight, the dict-based version, is deprecated and emits a DeprecationWarning.

docs.title: Validate a file
docs.text:
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = Path(tmp) / "my_claims.ttl"
    path.write_text(claim_ttl)

    g = rdflib.Graph()
    g.parse(path, format="turtle")
    conforms, report = validate_graph(g)
    if not conforms:
        print(report)

docs.title: Regenerate the schema artefacts
docs.text:
From a checkout of the repository:

uv sync --frozen --extra codegen
make gen             # src/indicium/generated/: model.py, shapes.ttl, ontology.ttl, schema.json
make context         # src/indicium/schema/context.jsonld, from the LinkML URI bindings
make schema-assets   # make gen and make context, then copy the artefacts and the changelog into docs/

The Turtle output is canonicalised, so a second run is byte-identical to the first.

docs.title: SEPIO evidence links and skill reliance
docs.text:
Indicium 2.0.0 corrects two SEPIO bindings before its first package release. The JSON keys stay the same; their RDF predicates change. The LinkML schema defines both bindings, and the packaged JSON-LD context is generated from it.

JSON key RDF predicate in 2.0.0 Meaning supports_claim sepio:0000427 (is_evidence_line_for) Evidence line → the Claim it evaluates for_claim indicium:for_claim Local evidence-line-to-Claim link asserts indicium:asserts Downstream skill or consuming resource → a Claim it relies on

Here sepio:, ro: and eco: expand to http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SEPIO_, http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_ and http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ECO_. The packaged context marks these underscore-ending bases with @prefix: true for JSON-LD 1.1 expansion.

docs.title: Why these bindings fit
docs.text:
The SEPIO ontology, whose version IRI is the 2023-06-13 release, declares sepio:0000006 (has_evidence_line) as the inverse of sepio:0000427. Its domain is the union of proposition (sepio:0000000) and assertion (sepio:0000001); its range is evidence line (sepio:0000002). Reversing that relation therefore gives an evidence line → proposition or assertion link. Indicium's Evidence already binds to the evidence-line class, and a Claim describes the scientific proposition being evaluated. This selection does not add an OWL equivalence between asb:Claim and either SEPIO class.

The old supports_claim binding, sepio:0000007 (has_supporting_evidence_line), is a subproperty of has_evidence_line and runs in the other direction. sepio:0000376 (evidence_item_for) links an evidence item to an evidence line, so it does not fit an Evidence → Claim edge. sepio:0000440 and sepio:0000441 also run from an assertion toward evidence, rather than from an evidence line toward a Claim.

The old asserts binding, sepio:0000130 (authored_by), concerns the agent that generated information. A skill can rely on a Claim without authoring it. sepio:0000030 (asserts_proposition) requires a SEPIO assertion as its subject, while sepio:0000109 (expresses) describes a document stating a proposition or assertion in its content. Neither captures reliance alone. indicium:asserts consequently has no external equivalence or close mapping. It is a schema-declared extension slot with range Claim; the core model does not introduce a Skill class or attach this slot to Claim.

The regression fixture in tests/fixtures/sepio/ preserves the relevant OWL axioms and lists its source version, SHA-256 and CC BY 3.0 attribution.

docs.title: Target and evidence direction
docs.text:
supports_claim retains its historical name and its LinkML alias for_claim. They refer to the same intended target but remain two independent JSON fields and two distinct RDF predicates. If both are populated, callers should use the same Claim IRI. The generated model does not copy one field into the other or enforce agreement. Neither field alone establishes supporting polarity.

Direction belongs on the evidence line as sepio:0000183, with one of:

Value Direction sepio:0000403 supporting sepio:0000404 disputing sepio:0000405 inconclusive

For example, a disputing line still identifies the Claim it evaluates:

@prefix asb: <https://w3id.org/asb#> .
@prefix indicium: <https://w3id.org/indicium/> .
@prefix sepio: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SEPIO_> .

<urn:example:claim> a asb:Claim ;
    asb:context "in vitro" ; asb:subject "A" ;
    asb:qualifier "inhibits" ; asb:relation "inhibits" ; asb:object "B" .
<urn:example:evidence> a sepio:0000002 ;
    sepio:0000427 <urn:example:claim> ;
    sepio:0000183 sepio:0000404 ;
    indicium:quote_exact "A does not inhibit B" .
<urn:example:skill> indicium:asserts <urn:example:claim> .

A SEPIO exporter may additionally emit the inverse claim sepio:0000006 evidence. Only when the evidence direction is known to be supporting may it use claim sepio:0000007 evidence. Do not reverse an old incorrect triple mechanically and infer support from the JSON key's name. An absent direction remains unspecified.

docs.title: ASB validation annotations
docs.text:
ASB's validation bridge already emits sepio:0000183 with the three direction values above, and ro:0002558 → eco:0000501 for automatic assertion evidence. These annotations are unchanged. They are separate from Indicium's Claim lifecycle (claim_status) and ECO evidence classification (eco_code).

@prefix asbval: <https://w3id.org/asb/validation#> .
@prefix sepio: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SEPIO_> .
@prefix ro: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_> .
@prefix eco: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ECO_> .

<urn:example:assessment> a asbval:ClaimAssessment ;
    sepio:0000183 sepio:0000403 ;
    ro:0002558 eco:0000501 .

The core LinkML model has no dedicated ASB assessment class or direction slot. Non-closed SHACL permits these external annotations but does not validate their values on assessment nodes. ASB owns that validation contract and its assessment-class alignment to SEPIO's evidence-line domain. Passing Indicium SHACL does not certify an ASB validation record. sepio:0000174 denotes the statement class, not a qualifier property.

https://w3id.org/indicium/context.jsonld does not resolve yet; the URI scheme page says where to load the context from until it does.

docs.title: Updating consumers
docs.text:
Keep JSON keys supports_claim, for_claim and asserts. Refresh embedded context copies from indicium-standard 2.0.0, then regenerate RDF that was expanded with the earlier context. In such old RDF, Evidence → Claim edges using SEPIO_0000007 need SEPIO_0000427, and skill-reliance edges using SEPIO_0000130 need indicium:asserts. Restrict any migration to those known uses: legitimate claim-side support and authorship triples must retain their SEPIO predicates. Records referring to the central context need no key rewrite; their expanded RDF and any cached context still need refreshing.

The packaged context is available without an HTTP request through importlib.resources.files('indicium.schema').joinpath('context.jsonld'). See URI scheme for namespace documentation and instance IDs.

docs.title: URI scheme
docs.text: This page records which IRIs Indicium uses, which of them resolve today, and what the pending registration will add. Every status below was measured on 2026-10-30.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
Prefix Namespace What it names Resolves today asb: https://w3id.org/asb# asb:Claim and eight slot IRIs: the SuperPattern slots asb:context, asb:subject, asb:qualifier, asb:relation, asb:object, and asb:domainQualifier, asb:sourceTaskKind, asb:workflowCoupling Yes asbval: https://w3id.org/asb/validation# Validation assertion terms used by ASB beside asb:. Not a prefix of this schema Yes indicium: https://w3id.org/indicium/ The LinkML schema id, the indicium prefix of the JSON-LD context, and every class and slot without its own class_uri or slot_uri: claim metadata (claim_status, claim_type, source_excerpt), the evidence and source slots (eco_code, quote_exact, for_claim, of_source, ...), ClaimLink, CitationLink and IndiciumDocument. The SHACL shapes check 75 property paths under this namespace, and the OWL artefact names every class and slot under it No (404)

Code never needs to spell these strings. The bases are exported:

from indicium import ASB_BASE, INDICIUM_BASE, asb_term

ASB_BASE           # 'https://w3id.org/asb#'
INDICIUM_BASE      # 'https://w3id.org/indicium/'
asb_term("Claim")  # 'https://w3id.org/asb#Claim'

docs.title: https://w3id.org/asb# and https://w3id.org/asb/validation#
docs.text:
Registered on w3id.org on 29 October 2026 (perma-id/w3id.org#7017). The redirects lead to documents hosted by the lab, which negotiate the representation:

Request Redirect chain Final response https://w3id.org/asb, Accept: text/turtle 301 to /asb/, 303 to https://holobiomicslab.eu/ns/asb, 303 to asb.ttl 200 text/turtle https://w3id.org/asb, Accept: application/ld+json same, ending at asb.jsonld 200 application/ld+json https://w3id.org/asb, Accept: text/html same, ending at asb.html 200 text/html https://w3id.org/asb/validation, Accept: text/turtle 303 to https://holobiomicslab.eu/ns/asbval, 303 to asbval.ttl 200 text/turtle https://w3id.org/asb/validation, Accept: text/html same, ending at asbval.html 200 text/html

The fragment of a hash IRI never reaches the server: https://w3id.org/asb#Claim is looked up in the document returned for https://w3id.org/asb. Cite the w3id IRIs, not the holobiomicslab.eu addresses behind them; the redirect target can change, the identifier does not.

docs.title: https://w3id.org/indicium/
docs.text:
Not registered. https://w3id.org/indicium/ and every IRI under it return 404. The request files are ready in the repository, under docs/release/w3id-indicium/, and wait on two prerequisites: the repository must be public and GitHub Pages must be enabled. RELEASING.md lists the order.

The request files propose the rules below. They take effect only when the registration is merged, and they can change until then:

IRI Accept Target https://w3id.org/indicium/ and single-segment terms, for example .../IndiciumDocument text/turtle docs/schema-assets/indicium.owl.ttl on the main branch, via raw.githubusercontent.com same application/ld+json src/indicium/schema/context.jsonld on main, via raw.githubusercontent.com same anything else the documentation site, https://holobiomicslab.github.io/indicium/ .../context.jsonld any src/indicium/schema/context.jsonld on main, via raw.githubusercontent.com .../indicium.owl.ttl, .../indicium.shapes.ttl, .../indicium.schema.json any the file in docs/schema-assets/ on main, via raw.githubusercontent.com .../<X.Y.Z>/<one of those files> any the file at the tag v<X.Y.Z> .../claim/<uuid> and other multi-segment paths any 404 (no service resolves instances)

docs.title: Two names for one class in the generated artefacts
docs.text:
The SHACL shapes and the pydantic model use the class_uri and slot_uri of the LinkML source. They bind Claim and eight of its slots to asb: IRIs; Evidence, Source, Figure, Script, SoftwareEntity and DataAsset to SEPIO, FaBiO, DoCO and DCAT classes; the two selectors to Web Annotation (oa:) and SSSOMMapping to sssom:Mapping; a few slots to Dublin Core, PROV and SEPIO properties; and every other class and slot to its indicium: IRI. Of the 87 property paths in the shapes, 75 are under indicium: and 8 under asb:.

The OWL artefact, indicium.owl.ttl, is generated with the LinkML default that names each class and slot by its schema-native IRI under indicium:, including those bound elsewhere: it declares 60 IRIs typed owl:Class (classes, enums and enum values), 58 owl:DatatypeProperty and 34 owl:ObjectProperty under https://w3id.org/indicium/. The ontology document itself is https://w3id.org/indicium. Each class bound elsewhere carries skos:exactMatch to that IRI (indicium:Claim to asb:Claim, indicium:Evidence to SEPIO_0000002, ...); the slots carry no such mapping. Validate data against the SHACL shapes. Most properties they check are indicium: IRIs, so the pending /indicium registration matters for claim and evidence data, not only for document-level terms.

docs.title: Entity identifiers
docs.text:
Producers mint their own identifiers; Indicium does not allocate them. Producers may use identity IRIs such as:

https://w3id.org/indicium/claim/<uuid>
https://w3id.org/indicium/evidence/<uuid>
https://w3id.org/indicium/source/<uuid>
https://w3id.org/indicium/software-entity/<uuid>
  • <uuid> is a UUIDv4 from the producing pipeline.
  • The producing system allocates and stores its instances. Indicium provides no central store and no resolver for individual UUIDs. These IRIs are names, not addresses: no service dereferences them, and the proposed /indicium rules leave multi-segment paths unserved.
  • Some consumers cite <identity>@sha256:<hex> as an immutable citation identifier. The hash is meaningful only with the producer's documented canonicalization and the preserved payload; sorting JSON keys is not by itself a standard RDF canonicalization. This package does not compute or verify these hashes.

The KGmemory adapter separately emits urn:indicium:claim:<id>. URNs are identifiers, not HTTP addresses. Its http://kgmemory.org/ns# base is a legacy external dependency; do not infer current ownership or availability from its presence in an export.

docs.title: JSON-LD context
docs.text:
The context is docs/context.jsonld in the repository, identical to src/indicium/schema/context.jsonld, which ships in the wheel. It is generated from the class_uri, slot_uri and enum meanings of the LinkML source (make context), so its term IRIs are the ones the SHACL shapes check. No public URL serves it today. Until one does, load it from the installed package:

from importlib.resources import files

context = (files("indicium") / "schema" / "context.jsonld").read_text()

After the release it will be served by the documentation site at https://holobiomicslab.github.io/indicium/context.jsonld and, once registered, at https://w3id.org/indicium/context.jsonld.

docs.title: Related identifiers of the same lab
docs.text:
Namespace Owner Resolves today https://w3id.org/holobiomicslab/asb-skill/... asb-skill-collections Yes. Registry, contributors, leaderboard and collection paths have their own rules; every other path redirects (302) to the repository https://w3id.org/holobiomicslab/asb-tool/... asb-skill-collections Redirects (302) to the same repository; there is no dedicated rule yet

An ASB-Tool IRI may appear as the value of SoftwareEntity.identifier, so one tool can be both a node in an Indicium graph and a citable release record.

docs.title: Stability
docs.text:
• A term IRI never changes after a tagged release. Published data embeds it.
  • Adding a class, a slot or an enum value is a minor version.
  • Changing an IRI, removing a slot, or tightening a cardinality is a major version. This is why the move of the asb: base to https://w3id.org/asb# was 2.0.0.

docs.title: ASTRA Adapter
docs.text:
Projects an Indicium claim onto an ASTRA Insight dict.

Use the typed bridge

indicium.astra_bridge.claim_to_insight(claim, evidence_doi=...) takes a typed Claim and needs the astra extra (pip install "indicium-standard[astra]"). The dict-based indicium.adapters.astra.claim_to_insight described below is deprecated and emits a DeprecationWarning. The bridge also reads ASTRA files back into claims: insight_to_claim, load_astra_findings, load_astra_prior_insights.

docs.title: Function
docs.text:
from indicium.adapters.astra import claim_to_insight

insight = claim_to_insight(claim)

The 5-slot SuperPattern is flattened into a single claim string. Evidence records map to ASTRA evidence entries (doi or artifact + optional quote). This is a lossy projection — full typing is preserved in the RDF/RO-Crate forms.

docs.title: Mapping
docs.text: ASTRA field Indicium source id claim["id"] claim "{subject} {relation} {object} ({context})" evidence[].doi evidence[].doi evidence[].artifact evidence[].artifact evidence[].quote.exact evidence[].quote

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from indicium.adapters.astra import claim_to_insight

claim = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "evidence": [{"doi": "10.1234/x", "quote": "A inhibited B by 80%."}],
}

insight = claim_to_insight(claim)
# {
#   "id": "c001",
#   "claim": "compound A inhibits growth of cell line B (in vitro)",
#   "evidence": [{"doi": "10.1234/x", "quote": {"exact": "A inhibited B by 80%."}}]
# }

docs.title: KGmemory Adapter
docs.text:
In preparation

The KGmemory adapter documentation will be published here when the KGmemory standard is publicly released.

A claim_jsonld() adapter for KGmemory is implemented in src/indicium/adapters/kgmemory.py and ships with this package. It emits a JSON-LD node referencing the KGmemory namespace (http://kgmemory.org/ns#SemanticMemory) so an Indicium claim is ingestible when KGmemory adopts the vocabulary.

docs.title: ASB task card adapter
docs.text: Projects an Indicium Claim dict onto an EvidenceSnippet dict, the evidence structure embedded in the task cards that AgenticScienceBuilder (ASB) produces. The target structure is the EvidenceSnippet class of the ASB task card schema, asb_schema/asb_card.yaml in the asb-schema package (asb-schema>=0.4.0). The module keeps its earlier name, indicium.adapters.scitask, so that existing imports keep working.

docs.title: Function
docs.text:
from indicium.adapters.scitask import claim_to_evidence_snippet

snip = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim)
# or with an explicit source path:
snip = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim, source_path="results/fig1.png")

docs.title: Mapping
docs.text: EvidenceSnippet field Indicium source snippet_id claim["id"] source_path First evidence[].artifact, then "doi:<doi>", then "" reason "{subject} [{qualifier}] {relation} {object} (context: {context})" text claim["source_excerpt"], then first evidence[].quote, then ""

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from indicium.adapters.scitask import claim_to_evidence_snippet

claim = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "source_excerpt": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.",
    "evidence": [{"doi": "10.1234/x", "artifact": "results/fig1.png"}],
}

snip = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim)
# {
#   "snippet_id": "c001",
#   "source_path": "results/fig1.png",
#   "reason": "compound A [inhibits] inhibits growth of cell line B (context: in vitro)",

docs.title: Indicium brand kit
docs.text:
Mark files for the Indicium standard.

The mark is a record sheet with three claim lines, bound by a round seal at its lower corner. It is the sibling of the AgenticScienceBuilder (ASB) crane mark: same palette, same stroke weights, no crane and no wordmark. The ASB brand kit (assets/brand/BRAND.md in asb-skill-collections) holds the ASB files; this folder holds the Indicium ones.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Brand folder: docs/assets/brand/.

File Content Ground indicium-mark.svg mark only, 256 x 256 square light indicium-mark-dark.svg mark only, 256 x 256 square dark indicium-mark-512.png indicium-mark.svg at 512 x 512 px, transparent light

Which file where:

Place File README header indicium-mark.svg with indicium-mark-dark.svg Documentation site header (CNRS blue bar in both schemes) indicium-mark-dark.svg Documentation site home page indicium-mark.svg with indicium-mark-dark.svg Browser tab indicium-mark-512.png Tools that refuse SVG indicium-mark-512.png

Both SVGs have a viewBox, no embedded raster, no <text> element, no external font and no external reference. Each carries a <title> and a <desc>.

docs.title: Palette
docs.text:
The palette is the one of the ASB brand kit.

Token Hex Role navy #00284b sheet and claim lines on light grounds (CNRS blue) blue-ink #001833 dark page ground blue-soft #0d3a66 secondary navy orange #e06c0a seal on light grounds orange-dark #f5923a seal on dark grounds paper #fbf7ef light page ground; sheet and claim lines on dark grounds paper-2 #f3ecdc inset surfaces, code blocks ink #16242f body text mute #5d6a78 secondary text on light grounds mute-dark #aebccb secondary text on dark grounds yellow #ffeb6e CNRS accent; not used in the mark yellow-soft #fff5a6 highlight; not used in the mark teal #04919a links on the documentation site; not used in the mark

The mark uses two colours per ground: navy and orange on light, paper and orange-dark on dark.

Contrast (WCAG 2):

Pair Ratio navy on white 14.95 navy on paper 13.99 orange on white 3.32 orange on paper 3.11 paper on #0d1117 17.71 paper on navy 13.99 orange-dark on #0d1117 8.16 orange-dark on navy 6.44

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
The mark carries no text. Pages and slides that set the name next to it use the type of the ASB brand kit:

Use Font Text and interface IBM Plex Sans Headings on the documentation site IBM Plex Serif Code IBM Plex Mono

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text:
• The mark is drawn on a 256-unit square.
  • Strokes: 7 units for the sheet outline, the folded corner and the three claim lines. Round caps and joins.
  • The seal is a filled shape: a ring 5 units wide around a scalloped disc of 16 lobes. The sheet outline stops short of the seal on the bottom and right edges, so the seal reads in front of the sheet.

Do not stretch, rotate, outline or recolour the files. Do not add shadows or gradients. Do not put the light files on dark grounds.

docs.title: GitHub README snippet
docs.text:
The <picture> element picks the source that matches prefers-color-scheme. The <img> falls back to the light file.

<p align="center">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/assets/brand/indicium-mark-dark.svg">
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="docs/assets/brand/indicium-mark.svg">
    <img alt="Indicium mark" src="docs/assets/brand/indicium-mark.svg" width="120">
  </picture>
</p>

docs.title: Schema Overview
docs.text:
The Indicium schema has one LinkML source of truth: src/indicium/schema/indicium.yaml

From it, four artefacts are generated:

Artefact Purpose generated/model.py Pydantic v2 models for Python consumers generated/schema.json JSON Schema for any language generated/shapes.ttl SHACL shapes for RDF validation generated/ontology.ttl OWL ontology for semantic alignment

docs.title: Core classes
docs.text:
Claim
 └── evidence: list[Evidence]
      └── of_source: Source

CitationLink   (connects two Claims or a Claim to a Source)

docs.title: The binding
docs.text: The one thing Indicium mints is the binding: a claim → typed evidence → a source, provenance-stamped. The claim structure is borrowed from Bucur et al.; the value Indicium standardizes is the typed grounding of claims in evidence.

docs.title: Claim
docs.text: A scientific claim expressed using the Bucur et al. (K-CAP 2021) 5-slot SuperPattern.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text: Slot Required Ontology Description id yes dct:identifier Stable claim identifier (string, UUID, or URN). Note: LinkML's identifier: true generates sh:maxCount 1 in SHACL but not sh:minCount 1; id is enforced as required by the Pydantic model and JSON Schema instead. context yes asb:context The experimental or conceptual setting subject yes asb:subject What the claim is about qualifier one of qualifier or domain_qualifier asb:qualifier Directional relation from the 20-term vocabulary domain_qualifier one of qualifier or domain_qualifier asb:domainQualifier Open snake_case term contributed by a domain adapter relation yes asb:relation Free-text relation elaboration object yes asb:object The target entity claim_type no — explicit or implicit source_excerpt no — Verbatim text from the source

docs.title: SuperPatternQualifier vocabulary
docs.text: 20 terms from Bucur et al.: causes, prevents, inhibits, activates, increases, decreases, correlates_with, is_associated_with, predicts, interacts_with, produces, requires, enables, treats, enhances, reduces, has_property, is_part_of, is_a, consistent_with.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
claim = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "claim_type": "explicit",
    "source_excerpt": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.",
}

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
An Evidence record grounds a Claim in a typed source.

Slot Required Ontology Description evidence_type no ECO Type of evidence (see table below) source_type no DoCO/IAO Type of source document or artefact quote no — Verbatim passage from the source confidence no — Float 0–1 of_source no — The Source this evidence points to for_claim no — The Claim this evidence grounds

docs.title: EvidenceType (ECO-mapped)
docs.text: Value ECO IRI data ECO:0000006 citation ECO:0000033 knowledge ECO:0000302 inference ECO:0000361 speculation ECO:0000034

docs.title: SourceType (DoCO/IAO-mapped)
docs.text: Value IRI text IAO:0000311 figure doco:Figure table doco:Table image IAO:0000536

docs.title: CitationLink
docs.text:
A CiTO-typed link from a source to a claim.

Slot Ontology Description link_type CiTO Relation type (see table below)

docs.title: LinkType (CiTO-mapped)
docs.text: Value CiTO IRI supports cito:supports disputes cito:disputes qualifies cito:qualifies citesForInformation cito:citesForInformation

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
A Source is a DoCO/FaBiO-typed document or artefact that an Evidence record points to.

Slot Required Ontology Description identifier yes dct:identifier DOI, URL, or local path title no dct:title Human-readable title authors no — List of author names license_id no — SPDX license identifier

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
source = {
    "identifier": "10.1234/test",
    "title": "Inhibition study of compound A",
    "authors": ["Smith J", "Doe A"],
}
